quandoUsar: A handful of pending notifications on a panel or dashboard, stacked to take little space and opened into a list when the person gets close.
Notifications that resolve by dismissing: drag the card sideways, a close button, or the `Delete` key.
quandoEvitar: Use `toast-stack` for transient results that appear at the screen edge and disappear on their own.
Use `notification-center` when you need read and unread state, a filter, and bulk actions behind a bell.
Use `swipe-actions` when the sideways gesture should reveal actions on a list row, and not remove the item.

teclado.acao: When entering the stack by keyboard it opens into a list; each card has one stop, on the dismiss button.
Dismiss the focused card and move focus to the next card, or to the “Bring them back” button when the stack empties.
Activate the focused button: dismiss a card, pin the list open (“Show all”), or clear everything (“Clear all”).

acessibilidade: With the stack closed, the cards behind are `aria-hidden` and out of the Tab order; the “Show all” button pins the list open and exposes `aria-expanded`.
A hidden `role="status"` announces how many notifications remain, each close button has an `aria-label` with the card's title, and the unread dot carries the text “Unread” for screen readers.
Dragging is not the only path: the close button and `Delete` do the same, and on touch screens a tap on the stack opens it.
movimento: Closed, each card behind shows 10 px and shrinks 5%; with the mouse over it, keyboard focus, or a pinned list, the cards drop into a list on a spring and the container height follows.
A dismissed card slides toward the drag side and disappears, and the others move up to close the line on a spring; dragging past 110 px or releasing above 650 px/s confirms the exit.
With “reduce motion” on, dragging is turned off, cards only fade out when leaving, and positions change instantly.
responsivo: The width is `min(25rem, 100%)` and each card's text is clipped to two lines, which keeps all of them the same height.
The open list grows downward in the page flow and pushes what comes after; `touch-action: pan-y` lets vertical scrolling through while the sideways drag dismisses.
desempenho: All notifications stay mounted, even those that do not show in the stack, each with its own `ResizeObserver` and drag; the block was designed for few items, not hundreds.
notasIA: Import the named component `NotificationStack`; the default export is the preview with example notifications.
Control it with `notifications` and `onNotificationsChange` (list from newest to oldest) or use `defaultNotifications`; `onDismiss(id)` fires per card, including for each one in “Clear all”.
In controlled mode also pass `defaultNotifications`: the empty state's “Bring them back” button returns that list and, without it, hands the example notifications to your `onNotificationsChange`.
